title: Stalks of the direct image of the constant sheaf of sets on a closed subset
statement: Let $T$ be a topological space, $C\subseteq T$ a closed subset and $R$ a set. Let $\mathcal L=(i_C)_*\underline R_C$ be the presheaf of sets on $T$ with $\mathcal L(V)=\{$locally constant maps $V\cap C\to R\}$ for $V\subseteq T$ open ($V\cap C$ with the subspace topology; a map is locally constant if every point has an open neighbourhood on which it is constant), the restriction maps being restriction of maps. For $x\in T$ let $\mathcal L_x=\varinjlim_{V\ni x}\mathcal L(V)$ be its stalk, the colimit of sets [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] over the open neighbourhoods $V$ of $x$ ordered by reverse inclusion, with germs $g\mapsto g_x$. Then: (0) $\mathcal L$ is a sheaf of sets on $T$; (a) for every $x\in C$ there is exactly one map $\mathrm{ev}_x:\mathcal L_x\to R$ with $\mathrm{ev}_x(g_x)=g(x)$ for every open $V\ni x$ and every $g\in\mathcal L(V)$, and $\mathrm{ev}_x$ is bijective; (b) for every $x\in T\setminus C$ the stalk $\mathcal L_x$ has exactly one element.

proof.text: For each open V in T, define L(V) as the locally constant maps from V intersected with C to R. Compatible maps on an open cover glue pointwise; local constancy is checked in the member containing each point. Uniqueness is pointwise, so the resulting presheaf is a sheaf by the locally constant maps sheaf node.

Fix x in C. Every open neighbourhood W of x in C is V intersected with C for some open neighbourhood V of x in T, and restricting V in T restricts W in C. Conversely, equality of two sections after restriction to a neighbourhood W in C implies equality after restriction to its representing neighbourhood V in T. Therefore the germ equivalence relation for L at x is exactly the germ equivalence relation for locally constant maps on C. The map taking a representative g on V to its restriction on V intersected with C identifies these two stalks. Under this identification, the evaluation map is the evaluation map of the locally constant germ node applied to U = C: it is well defined, bijective and uniquely determined by evaluation of representatives.

For x outside C, the open complement of C is a neighbourhood of x and has empty intersection with C, so it carries the unique empty map. Restricting any germ to a smaller neighbourhood inside this complement gives that map; hence the stalk is a singleton.
